param.name: mode
param.label: Analysis
param.option: Search skymaps (sky position, GRB and neutrino coincidences)
Parameter estimation plots of one event
Electromagnetic counterpart in the GW posterior
Primordial black holes: limits on the dark-matter fraction
Black hole in a scalar-field cloud (best fit)
GW170817 PE bundle from the GWTC-1 products

param.label: Catalogs
param.help: Catalog keys, space-separated (e.g. GWTC-1 GWTC-2.1 GWTC-3 GWTC-4 GWTC-4.1 GWTC-5). ALL takes them all except the updates (GWTC-4.1, update of GWTC-4), which are used only when named.

param.label: Include the detector networks
param.help: Include detector network via GWOSC v2 calls.

param.label: Include the sky areas
param.help: Compute sky localization area Axx if skymaps are available.

param.label: Credible level of the sky area
param.help: Credible level for sky area: 0.9→A90, 0.5→A50, 0.95→A95.

param.label: Data repository
param.help: Where the skymaps are read from: zenodo (the release tarballs); s3 (the MinIO mirror, faster) or galaxy (staged collections, else the public usegalaxy.org history), when they hold the maps of the selected release version, else Zenodo (a staged collection must hold them).

param.label: Zenodo release versions
param.help: Read an older Zenodo release version of a catalog instead of the latest, with any --data-repo (e.g. --zenodo-version GWTC-3=v2 GWTC-4=v1). Versions are numbered from the oldest (v1); list them with the zenodo_releases mode.

param.label: Catalogs
param.help: Catalog keys, space-separated (e.g. GWTC-1 GWTC-2.1 GWTC-3 GWTC-4 GWTC-4.1 GWTC-5). ALL takes them all except the updates (GWTC-4.1, update of GWTC-4), which are used only when named.

param.label: Credible level
param.help: Credible-level threshold (0–1). Common values: 0.9, 0.5, 0.95.

param.label: Sky-map analysis (label)
param.help: Analysis whose skymap is used, one per event (default: Mixed; without one, Mixed, then IMRPhenomXPHM_SpinTaylor, the GWTC-5.0 case, then the other waveforms in a fixed order). 'any': every map of every event; with --counterparts, one map per event, as Mixed.

tool.help:
GWTC analysis =============
This tool runs **gwtc_analysis** on the public data of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalogs (GWTC-1 to GWTC-5.0): event lists from GWOSC, parameter-estimation files and skymaps from the Zenodo releases, and the LVK search-sensitivity injections.
Analyses --------
* **Catalog statistics** (``gwtc_analysis catalog_statistics``): Build per-event TSV table and HTML summary report (with PIE plots) from GW catalogs. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/catalog-statistics/>`__ * **Event selection** (``gwtc_analysis event_selection``): Select GW events based on physical criteria (mass, distance, spin, source class) and write a TSV. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/event-selection/>`__ * **Search skymaps (sky position, GRB and neutrino coincidences)** (``gwtc_analysis search_skymaps``): Search GW sky localizations for a given sky position (RA/Dec), or for GRB and neutrino coincidences. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/search-skymaps/>`__ * **Parameter estimation plots of one event** (``gwtc_analysis parameters_estimation``): Generate parameter-estimation plots (posteriors, strain, waveforms) for one event. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/parameters-estimation/>`__ * **Merger rates (BNS, NSBH, BBH)** (``gwtc_analysis rates``): Estimate BNS / NSBH / BBH merger rates (per Gpc^3 per year) from the catalogs. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/rates/>`__ * **Hubble constant: bright siren** (``gwtc_analysis hubble_constant --method bright``): Hubble constant from an event with an identified host galaxy (bright siren). `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/hubble-constant-bright/>`__ * **Hubble constant: joint posterior** (``gwtc_analysis hubble_constant --method joint``): Joint Hubble-constant posterior of independent results. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/hubble-constant/>`__ * **Electromagnetic counterpart in the GW posterior** (``gwtc_analysis counterpart``): Where an electromagnetic counterpart sits in the GW posterior: sky, distance, viewing angle. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/counterpart/>`__ * **Neutron-star equation of state** (``gwtc_analysis neutron_star_eos``): Constrain the neutron-star equation of state jointly from GW170817 and GW190425 (Lambda_1.4, R_1.4). `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/neutron-star-eos/>`__ * **BBH effective-spin population** (``gwtc_analysis spin_population``): Infer the BBH effective-spin distribution and its correlation with the mass ratio. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/spin-population/>`__ * **Strongly lensed pairs** (``gwtc_analysis lens_pairs``): Screen every pair of BBH events for strong lensing (posterior overlap and time delay). `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/lens-pairs/>`__ * **Predicted compact-binary background** (``gwtc_analysis stochastic``): Predict the background of unresolved compact binaries, Omega_GW(f), against the upper limit. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/stochastic/>`__ * **Primordial black holes: limits on the dark-matter fraction** (``gwtc_analysis primordial_black_holes``): Upper limits on the fraction of dark matter in primordial black holes, from the merger rates. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/primordial-black-holes/>`__ * **Hawking's area law with GW250114** (``gwtc_analysis area_law``): Test Hawking's area law with GW250114 (inspiral against ringdown, LVK data release). `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/area-law/>`__ * **Continuous-wave upper limits** (``gwtc_analysis continuous_waves``): Continuous waves: the LVK upper limits (known pulsars, all-sky, boson clouds) and a boson-mass band. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/continuous-waves/>`__ * **Black hole in a scalar-field cloud (best fit)** (``gwtc_analysis scalar_cloud --stages prepare fit report``): Is a binary black hole better fitted with a scalar-field cloud around it (IMRPhenomXPHM_Scalar)? `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/scalar-cloud/>`__ * **GW170817 PE bundle from the GWTC-1 products** (``gwtc_analysis build_unofficial_pe``): Build an unofficial PESummary-compatible PE bundle from locally cached source files. `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/unofficial-pe/>`__ * **Zenodo release versions** (``gwtc_analysis zenodo_releases``): List the Zenodo release versions of each catalog (for --zenodo-version). `Documentation <https://danielsentenac.github.io/gwtc_analysis/modes/../data-sources/>`__
Data repository ---------------
Every analysis that downloads files has a **Data repository** option: ``zenodo`` (the public sources), ``s3`` (a MinIO mirror) or ``galaxy`` (the public usegalaxy.org GWTC history). The files read are the same whatever the repository (the latest Zenodo release versions, or the one selected); a mirror that lacks a file falls back to Zenodo. Each HTML report lists the files read and the options of the run.
Outputs -------
An HTML report (plots embedded), the main table of the analysis, extra tables when the analysis writes several, and the plots as a collection.
